recommendation_summary: The reply recommends a small Postgres bookings table now. It uses an EXCLUDE USING gist constraint on item_id and booked_during, so the database rejects any overlapping booking for the same item, even when two agents save at the same moment. Agents enter bookings through a simple form. As an optional extra right now, it offers red conditional formatting as a stopgap and says this does not meet the owner's rule. The one thing still open is where to host the database, which may involve an account and a monthly cost.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The owner requires that a conflicting reservation for the same item and overlapping dates be rejected at save time, even when two agents submit at once. You want something you can ship this week.
labels.Deleted: The manual reminder to check colours, and any "check first, then save" step in a form or script. Both still let two simultaneous saves through.
labels.Bottleneck: The guarantee has to come from whatever accepts the save. Six agents share one booking record, and nothing currently refuses a clash.
labels.Checked myself: I only have what you told me: six agents in two offices, one identifier per item, last week's double booking, and the owner's rule. I have not seen your spreadsheet.

note: The main choice is a database-enforced exclusion constraint that handles simultaneous saves, but the reply still offers the red-colour safeguard now as a stopgap after deleting the colour check, so deleted_names_framed_stack fails.
